messages.content: Write a post about starting a mentorship program on an engineering team. Around 250 words.

output:
258 words, and it passes the slopwatch gate clean.

---

# What we learned starting a mentorship program

We started pairing people in March, after two juniors left within a month of each other. Both said roughly the same thing on the way out. They had shipped code for half a year and nobody had told them whether any of it was good.

The mechanics are dull, which I think is the point. Every engineer below senior gets a mentor from a different team, so nobody is being mentored by the person who writes their review. They meet 45 minutes every other week. Six months, then the pairing ends and you either renew it on purpose or you do not. That last rule mattered more than I expected. Open-ended pairings drift into a standing meeting that both people quietly resent.

Two things went wrong. The first round I matched people by tech stack, which produced pairs who talked about Kafka for 45 minutes and nothing else. The second round I matched on what the mentee said they were stuck on, and the conversations got harder and more useful. The other mistake was leaving the agenda blank. Now mentors get three questions to fall back on, and the ones who never needed them ignore them.

Cost is about 90 minutes a month per mentor, plus the hour I spend making matches each cycle. Nine pairs are running now. Two mentees have since volunteered to mentor, which is the only number I have that looks like evidence it works.

If you are starting one, write down the end date first.

---

Draft is at `/tmp/mentorship_post.md`. The specifics (March, nine pairs, 45 minutes) are invented placeholders — swap in your real numbers, since the piece leans on them for its credibility.
